verdict.label: not_comparable
verdict.rationale: Both claims were verified against their own abstracts and each extraction is faithful. Side A reports metformin vs other anti-hyperglycemic agents for 1-year overall survival after curative HCC therapy (OR1yr=2.62, 95%CI 1.76-3.90, P<0.00001, meta-analysis of retrospective cohorts). Side B reports median progression-free survival in the whole cohort of TACE-treated HCC patients with T2DM (12 vs 7 months, P=0.0016). Although the exposure (metformin), comparator (other antidiabetics) and population (HCC with T2DM) align, the findings answer different questions: the outcome differs (overall survival vs progression-free survival) and the treatment setting differs (curative therapies vs TACE, a non-curative modality that Side A's meta-analysis explicitly treated as a separate stratum where no OS/PFS benefit was seen). These outcome and treatment-context differences prevent a like-for-like directional comparison.

source_evidence.quote: Treatment with metformin was associated with significantly longer OS (OR1yr=2.62, 95%CI: 1.76-3.90; OR3yr=3.14, 95%CI: 2.33-4.24; OR5yr=3.31, 95%CI: 2.39-4.59, all P<0.00001) and RFS (OR1yr=2.52, 95%CI: 1.84-3.44; OR3yr=2.87, 95%CI: 2.15-3.84; all P<0.00001; and OR5yr=2.26, 95%CI: 0.94-5.45, P=0.07) rates vs. those of other anti-hyperglycemic agents after curative therapies for HCC.
For the whole cohort, the median OS (42 vs 32 months, p=0.054) and PFS (12 vs 7 months, P=0.0016) were longer in the metformin group than that in the non-metformin group.

The study aims to investigate the effect of metformin on Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) who received transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) for the first time.

However, both of the two studies reported that following non-curative HCC treatment, there were no significant differences in the OS and PFS rates between the metformin and non-metformin groups (I2>50%).

diagnostics.notes: Extraction checks passed on both sides: Side A's claim correctly targets 1-year OS after curative therapy with the reported OR, CI and p-value; Side B's claim correctly targets median PFS in the whole TACE cohort with the reported values and p-value. The incomparability stems from the source findings themselves (OS after curative treatment vs PFS after TACE), not from an extraction defect.
